item_verdicts.call_sites: verified 3 production call sites of the shared writer - dispatch.py:1408 (session-host notify), dispatch.py:10090 (spawn request), fleet_migrate.py:384 (migration request) - and one entry to _local_request at fleet_migrate.py:641.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 32b987406; the increment is the single commit 2e2f5d3fe: dispatch.py imports REQUEST_FIFO_NAME and binds FLEET_FIFO_NAME to it, adds ENOENT to the bounded retry set and generalises one operator message; fleet_migrate.py replaces its local os.open retry loop with a call to the shared writer, re-raising CrewError as MigrationError; the test file adds two tests.
item_verdicts.done_when: the reviewed node's done-when names the ten-file pytest gate; its manifest records that exact command at 2e2f5d3fe with 365 passed EXIT=0 (migration-fifo-reuse-gate.log), and the two tests added by this increment cover the delegation and the ENOENT retry each behaviour clause names.
item_verdicts.goal: the increment's goal - resolve the prior review's reuse finding by sharing the supervisor request writer - is met: fleet_migrate._local_request (fleet_migrate.py:375-385) now delegates to dispatch._write_fleet_request, and dispatch.FLEET_FIFO_NAME aliases fleet_supervisor.REQUEST_FIFO_NAME at dispatch.py:9956, so one writer and one FIFO literal serve every caller.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 13c902590, 3f72ea363, 32b987406, 2e2f5d3fe, head gate log revision 2e2f5d3fe with 365 passed EXIT=0, declared negative control red; baseline_suite and after_suite are empty so the node records no same-command base arm.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the increment touches only reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/fleet_migrate.py and tests/test_fleet_migrate_stand_up.py, all inside the reviewed node's declared grants and exactly the three paths this review's goal names.

justifications.durability: both added tests genuinely guard the increment. Reverting the ENOENT retry (dispatch.py:10044) in a scratch tree reddens test_shared_fifo_writer_retries_until_the_fifo_exists (1 failed, 9 passed); reverting the delegation to the pre-increment local os.open loop reddens test_local_supervisor_request_uses_the_shared_fifo_writer (1 failed, 9 passed). The delegation test patches import_module('reckon.crew.dispatch')._write_fleet_request, which the call-time import in _local_request resolves.
justifications.evidence: the head arm the manifest names runs the node's exact ten-file command at 2e2f5d3fe and reports 365 passed EXIT=0 (migration-fifo-reuse-gate.log); I reproduced tests/test_fleet_migrate_stand_up.py at head (10 passed, EXIT=0) and falsified both new tests in a scratch tree. The node records no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so its added-failure delta rests on a single head arm.
justifications.fit: fleet_migrate._local_request keeps the module's injected-callable idiom with a local import of the shared writer and CrewError, and adds no plan, version or ticket label to any symbol or comment. The new module-top edge dispatch -> fleet_supervisor exists solely to source one constant; fleet_supervisor does not import dispatch (its load reaches dispatch only under TYPE_CHECKING and in lazy in-function imports), so the edge introduces no cycle and the import was verified live.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the increment implements exactly the repair the prior review's follow-on finding called for: fleet_migrate._local_request delegates to dispatch._write_fleet_request rather than re-implementing the deadline-bounded non-blocking FIFO write, removing the second writer the finding named.
justifications.reuse: the prior review's reuse finding (8 of 20) is resolved: the repository now has one FIFO writer (dispatch._write_fleet_request) called by the session-host notify, the spawn request and the migration request, and one FIFO literal (fleet_supervisor.REQUEST_FIFO_NAME) that dispatch.FLEET_FIFO_NAME aliases, so the two names can no longer drift.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed file (reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/fleet_migrate.py, tests/test_fleet_migrate_stand_up.py) is inside the reviewed node's declared grants; the increment carries nothing outside the repair it was dispatched for.
